parts.text: Which claim correctly names the places?

options.text: Call $5.307$ a whole-number label only, and stop naming places.
$5$ is ones; $3$ is tenths; $0$ is hundredths; $7$ is thousandths, with the decimal point separating whole-number places from fractional places.
Read $5307$ as the number, because those digits form the longest printed string.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice that uses the decimal point and place value.

stem: Darsh writes the decimal $5.307$ on the board. He wants to name each digit by its place value around the decimal point.

part_answers.answer: The decimal point separates ones from tenths, so each digit to the right is tenths, hundredths, then thousandths in order.

teacher.key_rationale: Place value around the decimal point names ones, tenths, hundredths, and thousandths in order; treating the string as a whole number or refusing places misses that test.
